transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-02 16:00 PST | Duration 45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jared (Cobalt CTO), Priya (ML Eng), Laura (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya Patel from Redwood - I'll hand it over to Ethan for the demo in a sec. Real quick, can you confirm the goals for today?
[00:07] Jared: Yeah hi - main thing is to see how we could use Redwood Hosted API for chat features in our customer support flow, and get a sense for latency, cost tradeoffs, and whether we need Dedicated or can start hosted. Also security is a must - SOC2 and SSO are blockers.
[00:20] Maya: Great, that matches what I heard. Ethan?
[00:24] Ethan: Cool, thanks. I'll show a quick walk-through: simple chat generation, streaming responses, changing params (temp, top_p, max_tokens), and then we'll go into retries/backoff and rate limiting. I'll also point out Redwood Console bits.
[00:34] Ethan: Starting at the API level - here's the standard chat create call. We send messages as role/content pairs, you get either full response or you can stream. (small cough) I'm pasting a short code snippet - ps, transcription sometimes drops punctuation, so apologies if typos.
[00:48] [Ethan shares screen: code sample]
[00:51] Ethan: For streaming we open a single connection and Redwood sends chunks as they generate. This helps with perceived latency - partial tokens show up sooner. Example: set stream=true, then handle data events.
[01:06] Laura: Do you support SSE and websockets?
[01:09] Ethan: Currently SSE over HTTP/2 in our SDK, we also have websocket wrappers for some customers. SSE is simpler to integrate. There's a note in the console docs.
[01:18] Priya: How's token counting done for streaming? Do you get charged for partial tokens?
[01:22] Ethan: Charging is per final token generated; streaming doesn't double-bill - you get billed for the tokens in the final output. There can be slight rounding on edge cases, but it's in the console usage tab.
[01:33] [00:33 mark - slight cross talk] Jared: Ok, show us latency numbers for small prompts, we expect <200ms ideally for the first word.
[01:42] Ethan: Right. On our medium-size model, typical cold-first-token latency in us-west is around 120-180ms at low QPS. With caching of prefixes and warmed KV cache, you can get sub-100ms for repeated prompts. For strict SLAs you may want Dedicated with pinned hardware.
[01:58] Priya: You mentioned KV cache - is that the key value cache for transformers?
[02:02] Ethan: Yes, KV cache for autoregressive decoding; sometimes the transcriber writes it as K V cash, ha. We use prefix caching and also chunked KV to speed follow-ups.
[02:10] Maya: Quick note on model variants - Redwood exposes curated open models and verified performance profiles. If capacity is tight we can route to a compatible variant automatically.
[02:19] Ethan: Back to params - temperature, top_p, max_tokens. Temperature controls randomness (0 = greedy), top_p is nucleus sampling. For deterministic outputs we recommend temperature 0 and add stop sequences.
[02:33] Ethan: Demo: changing temperature from 0.7 -> 0.2 produces more focused answers. (some typing sounds) Streaming shows tokens arriving faster even if total generation time is same.
[02:48] Laura: For stop sequences - do you support multiple stops?
[02:51] Ethan: Yes, array of stops. Also structured output is supported - you can pass JSON schema for the model to follow which helps downstream parsing.
[03:02] Jared: On retries: we get occasional 429s from our current provider. How does Redwood handle retries and idempotency?
[03:08] Ethan: Good question. We recommend client-side retry with exponential backoff for 429/5xx, and use an idempotency key for request-level dedupe. Redwood also supports request dedupe server-side if you pass idempotency_key header. We showed a sample retry policy in the SDK: backoff 200ms * 2^n with jitter, up to N attempts.
[03:27] Priya: If a retry happens, will the model generate duplicate tokens or is it guaranteed not to double-run?
[03:33] Ethan: With idempotency keys it's guaranteed we won't double-run the same request server-side. Without it, clients may see duplicate outputs; that's why we push idempotency for resumable ops. Also for streaming you should handle partials: if you reconnect, either restart or use a resume token - the SDK supports resuming in certain cases.
[03:52] [04:00 timestamp] Ethan: Error handling: on 429 return Retry-After header with suggested pause. Redwood also returns structured error codes like rate_limited, model_oom, model_unavailable. You can map these to logic in your app.
[04:12] Jared: Can you throttle per-user or per-route? We need fine-grained rate controls.
[04:16] Ethan: In Hosted API you can configure per-api-key limits and usage quotas; Console lets you create route-level policies. For enterprise we can sync these with your auth system.
[04:26] Maya: Quick console glance - show the latency chart, tokens cost breakdown, and the per-route dashboard.
[04:31] [screen share: Redwood Console]
[04:34] Ethan: Here is a cost breakdown per token, streaming vs non-streaming shows similar totals but streaming reduces perceived latency. Console also surfaces default retry policy and you can set custom policies.
[04:45] Priya: Regarding security: SOC2 and SSO are must-haves. What docs can you share?
[04:50] Maya: We have an enterprise security pack - SOC2 Type II report, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration for Private deployments, SSO with SAML/SCIM. I'll send the security docs link after the call.
[04:59] Jared: Data residency - can you pin region? We have EU residency reqs for some customers.
[05:04] Maya: Hosted supports region selection for data processing; for strict residency you can move to Dedicated or Private where the control plane is under your VPC. We'll include region options in the POC scoping.
[05:15] Ethan: Back to performance: we recommend running a 5-run benchmark for your top 50 prompts to understand median p50/p95 latency and token cost. If you send us the sample prompt set we'll run it from our us-west cluster and share results.
[05:28] Priya: Ok, we'll share prompts and target QPS - probably 10-20 qps peak initially.
[05:33] Ethan: For 10-20 QPS, hosted should be fine, but we might recommend reserved capacity if you want guaranteed throughput and lower cost per token.
[05:41] Laura: Pricing - can you share ballpark numbers?
[05:44] Maya: Yes, I'll send the pricing sheet after the call and include an estimated cost example based on your prompt set once Ethan runs the benchmark. We have usage-based pricing and discounted committed tiers for Dedicated.
[05:55] Jared: Any red flags with hallucinations? We do a lot of product copy generation but need high factual accuracy.
[05:59] Ethan: For high accuracy use lower temperature, add context and grounding, and use reranking/quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize. We also support fine-tuning/adapter approaches for custom domain knowledge. For production, set up quality regression alerts tied to prompt evals.
[06:17] Priya: How does the SDK handle streaming reconnects? If the connection drops at token 42 of 150, what's the best practice?
[06:23] Ethan: Best practice: use idempotency keys to avoid duplicated runs, and client should attempt resume if supported. Otherwise restart the request and concatenate or use partial content heuristics. SDK exposes small helpers for chunked resumption in some models.
[06:36] [small laughter] Jared: You mentioned automatic fallback to compatible variants - how transparent is that?
[06:40] Ethan: Very - routing policy can be set by latency, cost, or region. Client observes a single API surface; we do variant mapping on the backend and include a header noting the actual model served if you want telemetry.
[06:55] Maya: Quick recap - we'll send pricing and security docs, Ethan will run the latency benchmark once you share prompts, and we'll schedule a 30m POC scoping with infra/security. Any other questions?
[07:07] Laura: Can you include a sample prompt template for support replies and suggestion for stop sequences?
[07:11] Ethan: Yes, adding that to the benchmark packet.
[07:14] Jared: Great, thanks everyone.
[07:16] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[07:20] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution, some tech terms slightly mangled (K V cash for KV cache), filler words present. Transcript aligns roughly with 45m call but condensed for highlights.

References shared: Redwood Console link (shared in chat), security pack link (to be sent), sample benchmark spreadsheet (SE will upload).
